title: Record Breakers
intro: The biggest, fastest and tallest things in nature and space. Can you spot the champions?

questions.prompt: What is the tallest mountain on Earth, measured from sea level?
questions.explanation: Mount Everest, on the border of Nepal and China, rises about 8,850 metres above sea level, higher than any other mountain.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest animal known to have ever lived?
questions.explanation: The blue whale is the largest animal known to have lived on Earth, bigger even than the largest dinosaurs.

questions.prompt: Which is the fastest land animal?
questions.explanation: Cheetahs are the fastest land mammals and can reach 60 to 70 miles an hour over short distances.

questions.prompt: Which is the tallest animal alive today?
questions.explanation: Giraffes are the world's tallest mammals. Their legs alone can be taller than many adult people.

questions.prompt: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.explanation: Mercury is the smallest planet and the one closest to the Sun.

questions.prompt: The emperor penguin is the largest kind of penguin.
questions.explanation: Emperor penguins are the tallest and heaviest of all penguins, standing about 115 centimetres tall.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest lizard in the world?
questions.explanation: The Komodo dragon is the biggest lizard alive and can grow up to about 3 metres long.

questions.prompt: A day on Jupiter, one full spin, lasts about how many Earth hours?
questions.explanation: Jupiter spins once about every 10 hours, faster than any other planet, so its days are very short.

questions.prompt: Which planet is the hottest in our solar system?
questions.explanation: Venus is the hottest planet. Its thick clouds trap heat, so it is even hotter than Mercury, which is closer to the Sun.

questions.prompt: The African elephant is the largest animal living on land.
questions.explanation: African elephants are the biggest land animals on Earth. Large adults can weigh several tonnes.
